kept.heading: REGISTER FOR THE WORKSHOP
61 MILLION CONSUMERS ASK AI WHAT TO BUY. THEN THEY BUY IT ON AMAZON (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 23% of US consumers, or roughly 61 million people, now start retail research with AI. Average AI-assisted spending rose 17% from $889 in June to $1,039 in August. Yet 60% of AI-assisted purchases still close on Amazon. In a controlled test, 40% of consumers chose a marketplace even when told other retailers offered the same product, price, shipping, and returns.

kept.heading: INSIDE MCDONALD'S NEW MARKETING MODEL AS IT ENTERS MEDIA NETWORK FRAY (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: McDonald's is piloting a media network across 450 US company-owned restaurants, selling ad space on its app, kiosks, and menu boards, with the goal of building a billion-dollar business. Its marketing is shifting to fewer, bigger global campaigns built on its own IP. It is roughly doubling spending on long-running programs about its brand and food quality while cutting short-term promotions.

kept.heading: HOW TO FIND REAL HUMAN STORIES FOR PR AND JOURNALISM (14 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands can strengthen PR pitches by pairing their data or news angle with a real customer or person who has experienced the issue firsthand. A strong human story gives journalists an interviewee who can provide specific details and memorable quotes that make the story more relatable. Brands can find these people through targeted social media searches and OSINT techniques, then offer the verified source to journalists as part of the pitch. Only 5% to 10% of people contacted cold on social media may respond, so you may need to contact many potential sources and verify each person carefully.

kept.heading: AI GUIDE TO BUILDING A TOP-TIER INBOUND AI AGENT (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: SaaStr's inbound AI agent held 17,000 conversations with prospects and booked about 600 meetings in a year. Together with a newer self-serve agent, it drove a 60% jump in new business, and three people created the whole setup. The on-site agent sits on the sponsor page, qualifies visitors on budget and goals, then books the meeting itself. For buyers who skip the chat, a second agent swaps the PDF prospectus for a page unique to each company. It checks first-party signals, then drafts a pitch that a human approves and that updates the same link in place.

kept.heading: IS THIS THE LAST PLACE TO AUTOMATE? (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Use AI to research prospects, but write the outreach yourself. Find a genuine connection on LinkedIn, tie it to a specific buyer problem, and address likely objections before they come up. Write 50 emails Monday through Wednesday, send them Thursday and Friday, then follow up within 48 hours over the weekend. On intro calls, skip generic discovery questions and let the buyer talk. If someone asks to reconnect later, respect the timing and nurture them with useful insights instead of “just checking in” messages.

kept.heading: HOW TO USE GOOGLE VEO TO CREATE VIDEO ADS FOR PMAX AND DEMAND GEN (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google Veo lets you turn existing static assets into 5 or 10 second video ads for Performance Max and Demand Gen campaigns. Strong, high resolution product images matter because the tool animates two images into sequential scenes and supports 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 formats. The two 30 character headlines should focus on the ad message rather than branding since the business name already appears first. Advertisers should test Veo as a low cost way to refresh creative and evaluate clicks and website engagement alongside conversions.

kept.heading: COGSEND (TOOL)
kept.blurb: CogSend is a free, open-source social media scheduler that lets you manage posts across Mastodon, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, and X from one place. You can write a post once, customize it for each platform, then publish or schedule it. It runs on your own Cloudflare account, so you keep control of your accounts and data without a monthly fee. The setup takes a few steps, with a demo video showing how to get it up and running.

kept.heading: HOW TO WIN AI SEARCH WITH CREATORS (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI answers lean on third-party voices, so less than 10% of what they say about a brand comes from the brand's own content. 1 in 3 answers cite creators directly. Follower count barely matters, since 57% of cited YouTube videos come from channels under 100K. This playbook recommends combining SEO keyword data with real customer questions to build a shared prompt list, picking creators for authority and specificity, and reposting content stuck behind Instagram and TikTok login walls to YouTube as transcripts that AI crawlers can reach.

kept.heading: HOW GOOGLE AND UBER MEASURE WHAT CANNOT BE RANDOMIZED (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Major marketing investments that can't be randomized still need causal measurement, rather than post-hoc narratives. Google's CausalImpact and Uber's synthetic control methods show how you can estimate the effect of national launches, sponsorships, and other whole market interventions by building counterfactuals from historical data or comparable markets. These methods are weaker than randomized tests, so you should preregister the analysis, establish a strong pre period, run placebo tests, and report uncertainty intervals. Synthetic control should be a last resort for spending that cannot support randomization.

kept.heading: IS THE TRADITIONAL MARKETING TEAM DYING, SHRINKING, OR TURNING INTO SOMETHING ELSE? (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The modern marketing team is built around three principles. 0-1 marketers use AI systems to take work from idea to shipped output with fewer handoffs. Pods replace traditional team hierarchies with small groups that share context, own a specific outcome, and ship and learn weekly. Depth of craft becomes more valuable as AI handles production, giving specialists more time to apply the judgment and expertise needed to make standout work.

kept.heading: YOUTUBE PROMISES CUSTOM FEEDS AND A LOT MORE AI LATER THIS YEAR (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Users will be able to create custom feeds around specific interests, while AI will play a bigger role in search and recommendations.

kept.heading: EVEN AMERICANS WHO USE AI EVERY DAY ARE WORRIED ABOUT IT (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: In Gallup's survey of 37 countries, the US was the most anxious, with 74% worried and only 36% expecting AI to mostly help the country.

kept.heading: CHATGPT ADS SEEM TO LIFT ORGANIC TRAFFIC. IS PAYING TO BE FOUND THE FUTURE OF AI SEARCH? (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: ChatGPT ads appear to coincide with higher organic ChatGPT traffic, but some of that lift may come from ad clicks being misclassified as organic referrals in GA4. OpenAI says ads don't influence its answers, and there is no public study proving whether ads affect organic visibility. It recommends tagging ad URLs, auditing ‘oppref' traffic, running holdout tests, and tracking organic mentions separately from traffic.

kept.heading: CLIPPING 101: INSIDE THE CLIPPING ECONOMY (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Clipping is emerging as a performance-based distribution model where brands pay networks of creators to turn existing content into short-form clips and only pay when posts reach verified view thresholds. The model has gained traction in entertainment, where brands have large libraries of inherently watchable content, while also serving as a way to test creative before putting paid spend behind the best-performing clips.

kept.heading: HOW TO USE CUSTOMER LANGUAGE FOR POWERFUL MARKETING COPY (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Pull customer language from 15 to 20 recent reviews, support tickets, sales calls, Google Ads search terms, and AI conversations. Tag phrases that repeat and use them in headlines, CTAs, ads, service pages, and FAQs. For AI visibility, ask prospects who found you through ChatGPT or Perplexity to share their conversations, including follow-up questions and competitor comparisons. Start by changing one headline or CTA, measure results after 30 days, then repeat quarterly.

kept.heading: HOW LONG SHOULD YOUR FREE TRIAL BE? (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Test trial length based on how quickly users experience value, how often they need to return, and the cost of free access. Compare short trials against 5-9, 10-16, and 17-32-day options within each subscription plan, tracking conversion and first renewal separately. For monthly plans, test 10-16 days rather than assuming longer is better. AI apps should also factor in per-user inference costs, while regional and category differences can justify different trial lengths.

kept.heading: AMAZON WILL LET SELLERS MANAGE WALMART, EBAY, SHOPIFY, AND TIKTOK SALES FROM THEIR AMAZON DASHBOARDS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Amazon is rolling out free multichannel selling tools that let US sellers manage Walmart, eBay, Shopify, and TikTok sales from Seller Central. Sellers can connect accounts, sync listings, view orders, and fulfill purchases across channels. Amazon says it will not use rival-platform data for other purposes.

kept.heading: HOW X'S RANKING ALGORITHM WORKS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: X's ranking algorithm favors posts that people are likely to share, reply to, or quote rather than simply like. A copy link share carries 40X the weight of a like, while replies and quotes each carry 10X the weight. Posts also need to stay focused on a clear topic to reach relevant nonfollowers, and negative actions such as mutes and reports carry heavy penalties. The algorithm also reduces the value of repeated posts from the same author and stops considering posts after 48 hours. Posting less often and creating highly shareable content can improve reach.

kept.heading: AI MARKETING IS MOVING INTO THE DATA PLATFORM (14 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Agentic CDPs bring AI directly into governed customer data, giving agents the context needed to build audiences and design campaigns. Unlike traditional CDPs that sync copies of data into marketing tools, they connect directly to the governed data platform and combine customer behavior with real-time signals and business goals. The use cases build over time, from natural-language data queries to agent-built campaigns and continuous engagement.

kept.heading: THE STACK LADDER: WHAT COMPANIES RUN AT 10, 50, 200, 1,000, AND 10,000 PEOPLE (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Startups don't necessarily switch to enterprise software as they grow. Among Y Combinator companies with 1 to 1,000 employees, the same category leaders dominate at most company sizes. HubSpot leads CRM at every size, while Cloudflare leads hosting, including among Fortune 500 companies. Marketo and Adobe Experience Manager appear only among Fortune 500 companies. What changes with headcount is adoption. CRM usage rises from 7% of the smallest startups' homepages to 42% among companies with 201 - 1,000 employees.

kept.heading: FISHWIFE SARDINES JUST ANNOUNCED THE QUIRKIEST COLLAB (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Dieux and Fishwife collaborated on reusable silicone eye patches featuring Fishwife's signature fish illustrations, packaged to look like a tin of fish.

kept.heading: 27 REAL SUBJECT LINE EXAMPLES FOR EVERY TYPE OF MEDIA PITCH (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Subject lines with key details in the first 3 words had a 46% open rate vs. 38% when it appeared in word 7 or later.

kept.heading: OPENAI BOTS MEDDLED WITH MULTIPLE US GOVERNMENT AGENCY SITES (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI said its AI agents improperly interacted with dozens of government and public agency websites, including the SEC and Census Bureau.
